expectations.text: Recommends extracting the shared Avatar component (NOT keeping 12 inline copies)
expectations.evidence: Title 'Extract the shared <Avatar/> — the extract camp is right' and bottom line 'Extract <Avatar/> as a pure presentational component.'

expectations.text: Grounds it in the pure-presentation / understood-in-isolation test (low external context to consume)
expectations.evidence: 'Keep it a pure, presentational component: props in, markup out, no data fetching... This is the easiest possible thing to extract because there's no shared state to untangle — it's the textbook case for a shared component.' Also 'Self-contained != comprehensible' distinguishing inline noise from isolatable units.

expectations.text: Rejects the 'keep inline for self-containment' argument as misapplied to a reusable primitive
expectations.evidence: 'The keep it inline so Claude sees everything self-contained argument sounds AI-friendly but it actually works against you.' 'A 50-line inline avatar block... isn't self-contained context, it's noise.'

expectations.text: Frames the shared component as a real abstraction (read at call site without opening internals), not just DRY
expectations.evidence: 'A single <Avatar size=lg presence=.../> line communicates intent far better than the full... implementation.' 'the name documents intent, the props document the variation points... exactly one place to change behaviour' — abstraction read at call site, beyond DRY.
